title: Widen the quantum box
hook: Change box width and predict energy eigenvalue.
misconception: energy eigenvalue doubles when box width doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply E_n = n²h²/(8mL²) to compare energy eigenvalue when box width changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a particle in a one-dimensional infinite square well with fixed mass and quantum number, E_n = n²h²/(8mL²). When box width doubles, energy eigenvalue becomes ¼ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model E_n = n²h²/(8mL²); scaling exponent -2. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a particle in a one-dimensional infinite square well with fixed mass and quantum number, with a nonzero initial result. If box width triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on energy eigenvalue?
recall.why: Apply E_n = n²h²/(8mL²) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/9.
